verifications.claim: The Fab Five were the 1991 University of Michigan men’s basketball recruiting class.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Fab Five was the 1991 University of Michigan men's basketball team recruiting class"
verifications.reasoning: Directly stated in the opening sentence of the main sources.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five consisted of Chris Webber, Jalen Rose, Juwan Howard, Jimmy King, and Ray Jackson.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: Photo caption: 'From left to right: Ray Jackson, Juwan Howard, Jalen Rose, Jimmy King and Chris Webber.' Listed identically across sources.
verifications.reasoning: Consistently named in all references as the five members.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five became the first all-freshman starting lineup to reach an NCAA Championship game.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "The Fab Five were the first team in NCAA history to compete in the championship game with all-freshman starters."
verifications.reasoning: Exact match to the historical fact stated.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five reached consecutive Final Fours in 1992 and 1993.
verifications.label: CLEAR
verifications.evidence: "They reached the 1992 and 1993 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Championship games as both freshmen and sophomores." "led the Wolverines to the Final Four in 1992 and 1993."
verifications.reasoning: Reaching championship games confirms Final Four appearances; explicitly stated.

verifications.claim: The Fab Five started all games as freshmen in 1992.
verifications.label: INCORRECT
verifications.evidence: 1991–92 stats: Rose 33/34 GS, Webber 34/34, Howard 31/34, King 21/34, Jackson 15/34. "At first, only three of the freshmen started... did not start regularly until February 9, 1992. ... started as a unit in all but one of the season's remaining games."
verifications.reasoning: Stats and text show not all five started all 34 games; starting as unit began late season.
